name: Breakup of Pangaea
summary: The supercontinent split into Laurasia and Gondwana; India drifted north and hit Asia ~50 million years ago.

name: Chicxulub asteroid impact
impact: ~75% of species lost, incl. non-avian dinosaurs
summary: A ~10 km asteroid hit Yucatán; mammals later inherited the Earth.

name: Onset of the Quaternary ice ages
summary: Ice sheets advanced and retreated about every 41,000, then 100,000 years.

name: Toba super-eruption
impact: Ash layer across India; debated effect on humans
summary: One of the largest eruptions in 2 million years; Indian sites like Jwalapuram suggest people survived it.

name: Last Glacial Maximum
impact: Sea level ~120 m lower; land bridges
summary: Humans crossed Beringia into the Americas around this time or after.

name: Younger Dryas
summary: A sudden 1,200-year chill, possibly from meltwater shutting the Atlantic circulation.

name: Quaternary megafauna extinction
impact: Mammoths, giant sloths, cave lions vanish
summary: Caused by human hunting combined with climate change.

name: End of the Green Sahara
summary: Drying pushed people into the Nile valley as Egypt's state formed.

name: 4.2-kiloyear drought
impact: Collapse of Akkad, Egypt's Old Kingdom; Indus decline
summary: Defines the start of the Meghalayan Age, named from a Meghalaya cave stalagmite.

name: Thera (Santorini) eruption
summary: One of the largest eruptions of human history.

name: Eruption of Vesuvius
summary: Preserved a Roman town frozen in time.

name: Volcanic winter of 536
impact: 'The worst year to be alive'; crop failures
summary: Followed by the Late Antique Little Ice Age and Justinian's plague.

name: Tambora eruption
summary: Caused famine in Europe; possibly linked to a new cholera strain in Bengal (1817).

name: Krakatoa eruption
summary: Its sound was heard 4,800 km away.

name: Plague of Athens
impact: Killed perhaps a quarter of Athens, including Pericles

name: Antonine Plague
summary: Brought back by soldiers from Mesopotamia.

name: Plague of Justinian
impact: Tens of millions dead over two centuries

name: Black Death
summary: Spread along Mongol trade routes; transformed labour and religion.

name: Smallpox in the Americas
impact: Up to ~90% of Indigenous people died
summary: Smallpox, measles and flu brought by Europeans.

name: Cholera pandemics
summary: The first pandemic began in the Ganges delta; John Snow traced cholera to water in 1854.

name: Third plague pandemic
summary: Bombay's 1896 plague led to harsh British measures; Yersin found the bacterium.

name: Spanish flu
summary: India suffered the most deaths of any country.

name: HIV/AIDS pandemic
summary: Antiretroviral drugs turned it into a manageable condition.

name: COVID-19 pandemic
summary: Led to lockdowns and record-speed vaccines.

name: Invention of writing
summary: Cuneiform and hieroglyphs started as accounting marks.

name: Unification of Egypt
summary: Narmer united Upper and Lower Egypt.

name: Battle of Kadesh
impact: Led to the first known peace treaty
summary: Ramesses II vs the Hittites, the largest chariot battle.

name: Buddha's enlightenment
summary: Siddhartha Gautama became the Buddha under the Bodhi tree.

name: Alexander's invasion of India
impact: Battle of the Hydaspes against Porus
summary: His army mutinied at the Beas.

name: Kalinga War
summary: Led Ashoka to spread Buddhism and dhamma.

name: Punic Wars
summary: Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants.

name: Roman conquest of Gaul
summary: Julius Caesar defeated Vercingetorix at Alesia.

name: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Christianity became Rome's state religion by 380.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
impact: Start of the Middle Ages in the West

name: Hijra and rise of Islam
summary: Prophet Muhammad moved from Mecca to Medina.

name: Arab conquest of Sindh
impact: Islam arrives in South Asia by land

name: Chola naval expedition to Srivijaya
summary: Rajendra Chola's navy raided Srivijaya's ports.

name: Battle of Hastings
summary: William the Conqueror defeated Harold II.

name: First Crusade
summary: The start of two centuries of crusades.

name: Second Battle of Tarain
impact: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj Chauhan
summary: Opened North India to the Delhi Sultanate.

name: Magna Carta
summary: An early step toward constitutional rule.

name: Sack of Baghdad
impact: End of the Abbasid Caliphate; House of Wisdom destroyed

name: Columbus reaches the Americas
summary: Connected the Old and New Worlds.

name: Vasco da Gama reaches India
impact: Sea route from Europe to India
summary: Began European colonial trade in Asia.

name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
summary: Cortés with Indigenous allies and smallpox.

name: Founding of the East India Company
impact: A trading company that conquered India
summary: Granted a royal charter by Elizabeth I.

name: Thirty Years' War
summary: Created the modern idea of state sovereignty.

name: Battle of Plassey
summary: Robert Clive defeated Siraj ud-Daulah through Mir Jafar's betrayal.

name: Third Battle of Panipat
impact: Marathas defeated by Ahmad Shah Durrani
summary: One of the bloodiest battles of the 18th century.

name: Great Bengal Famine
impact: ~10 million dead (about a third of Bengal)

name: French Revolution
impact: End of absolute monarchy; 'Liberty, equality, fraternity'

name: Haitian Revolution
impact: First nation founded by formerly enslaved people

name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
impact: End of Company rule; Crown takes over
summary: Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, Tantia Tope, Bahadur Shah Zafar.

name: Opium Wars
summary: Britain forced China to accept opium grown in India.

name: Abolition of slavery in the British Empire
summary: Indentured Indian labourers then went to Mauritius, Fiji, the Caribbean.

name: Scramble for Africa
summary: The Berlin Conference divided the continent.

name: Great Famine of 1876–78
summary: El Niño drought plus colonial grain policy.

name: Founding of the Indian National Congress
Russian Revolution
summary: Lenin and the Bolsheviks seized power.

name: Salt March
summary: Gandhi walked 390 km to Dandi to make salt.

name: World War II
summary: 2.5 million Indians served, the largest volunteer army.

name: The Holocaust
summary: Plus millions of Roma, disabled people and others.

name: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
summary: The only nuclear weapons used in war.

name: Indian Independence and Partition
impact: India and Pakistan created; ~15 million displaced, up to ~2 million killed
summary: One of the largest migrations in history.

name: Bangladesh Liberation War
summary: India intervened after a genocide and refugee crisis.

name: September 11 attacks
impact: ~3,000 killed; wars in Afghanistan and Iraq

name: 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
summary: Hit Tamil Nadu and the Andamans.

name: Chandrayaan-3 lands on the Moon
impact: First landing near the lunar south pole
summary: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.

name: Human–chimpanzee split
summary: Our ancestors diverged from those of chimpanzees, probably in a mosaic of forest and woodland.

name: First upright walking
summary: Ardipithecus walked upright on the ground but still climbed trees; leaving the forest canopy was gradual.

name: Laetoli footprints
summary: Three hominins walked through wet volcanic ash, leaving the oldest human-like footprints.

name: First stone tools (Lomekwi)
summary: Large stone cores and flakes made before the genus Homo appeared.

name: Oldowan toolmaking
summary: Sharp flakes let early humans cut meat and break bones for marrow.

name: Homo erectus leaves Africa
summary: Small-brained humans reached the Caucasus and soon East Asia.

name: Acheulean hand-axes
summary: The longest-lasting tool tradition, used for over 1.5 million years.

name: Controlled fire at Wonderwerk Cave
summary: Burned bones and plant ash show fire inside a cave a million years ago.

name: Regular hearths (Qesem Cave)
summary: Repeated hearth use shows fire had become part of daily life.

name: Schöningen spears
summary: Wooden throwing spears found with butchered horses.

name: Homo sapiens at Jebel Irhoud
summary: The oldest known Homo sapiens fossils.

name: Blombos Cave engravings
summary: Engraved ochre and shell beads show abstract symbols.

name: Arrival in Australia
summary: People crossed open water to reach Sahul.

name: Neanderthal–sapiens interbreeding
summary: Our ancestors mixed with Neanderthals, leaving ~1–2% of their DNA in most people today.

name: Oldest figurative cave art (Sulawesi)
summary: A painted scene of humans and a pig in Leang Karampuang.

name: Neanderthal extinction
summary: Small populations, competition and climate shifts ended the Neanderthals.

name: Chauvet Cave paintings
summary: Lions, rhinos and horses painted with shading and perspective.

name: Dog domestication
summary: Wolves became dogs alongside Ice Age hunters.

name: White Sands footprints
impact: Earliest firm evidence of people in the Americas
summary: Human footprints in ancient lake mud.

name: Clovis culture
summary: Fluted spear points spread across North America.

name: Natufian culture and first villages
summary: Hunter-gatherers harvested wild grains and built stone houses.

name: Göbekli Tepe built
summary: Carved stone pillars raised by hunter-gatherers.

name: Jericho walls and tower
summary: A stone tower and wall around an early farming town.

name: Rice cultivation in the Yangtze
summary: Shangshan and Hemudu villages grew rice.

name: Maize domestication
summary: Teosinte was bred into maize in the Balsas valley.

name: Horse domestication
summary: Ancient DNA shows today's horses descend from steppe horses domesticated around 4,200 years ago.

name: Wheel and wagon
summary: Solid wooden wheels appeared almost simultaneously across Eurasia.

name: Narmer unifies Egypt
summary: The Narmer Palette shows a king wearing both crowns.

name: Great Pyramid built
summary: Built for Khufu by organised paid crews.

name: Hyksos expelled from Egypt
summary: Ahmose I drove out Asian rulers.

name: Akhenaten's religious revolution
summary: A pharaoh promoted a single sun-disc god.

name: Trojan War (traditional)
summary: Excavations at Hisarlik show a destroyed city around this time.

name: Iron smelting spreads
summary: Cheap iron tools made farming and armies larger.

name: Olympic Games founded
summary: Held every four years for over 1,000 years.

name: Fall of Nineveh
summary: Babylonians and Medes destroyed the Assyrian capital.

name: Chandragupta–Seleucus treaty
summary: Seleucus traded lands for 500 war elephants.

name: Ashoka's edicts
summary: Rock edicts in Brahmi and Kharosthi.

name: Great Wall unified by Qin
summary: Earlier walls joined under Qin Shi Huang.

name: Silk Road opened (Zhang Qian)
summary: Han envoy Zhang Qian reached Bactria.

name: Yellow Turban rebellion
summary: Peasant revolt led to warlordism and the Three Kingdoms.

name: Huna invasions of India
summary: Toramana and Mihirakula attacked northern India.

name: Xuanzang's journey to India
summary: Studied at Nalanda and brought texts to China.

name: Tang–Tibet wars
summary: Songtsen Gampo's successors rivalled the Tang.

name: An Lushan rebellion
summary: One of the deadliest conflicts of pre-modern times.

name: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
summary: Monks massacred at a famous monastery.

name: Saladin retakes Jerusalem
impact: End of the Crusader kingdom's core

name: Great Famine of Europe
summary: Rain-ruined harvests at the start of the Little Ice Age.

name: Hundred Years' War
summary: Joan of Arc; the longbow at Agincourt.

name: Zheng He's voyages
summary: Treasure fleets reached Calicut and East Africa.

name: Battle of Grunwald
summary: One of medieval Europe's largest battles.

name: Fall of Granada and Reconquista
impact: End of Muslim rule in Iberia

name: Spanish Armada defeated
summary: Storms and fireships scattered the fleet.

name: Manchu conquest of China
summary: Ming collapsed after Li Zicheng's revolt.

name: Seven Years' War
impact: Britain dominates India and North America

name: Black Hole of Calcutta
summary: A disputed incident used in British propaganda.

name: Treaty of Allahabad
summary: The Company became Bengal's tax collector.

name: Latin American independence
summary: Bolívar and San Martín led wars of independence.

name: Abolition of sati
summary: Campaign led by Ram Mohan Roy.

name: Taiping Rebellion
summary: Led by a man claiming to be Jesus's brother.

name: Russo-Japanese War
impact: First Asian victory over a European power

name: Creation of Israel and the Nakba
Korean War
summary: An armistice, never a peace treaty.
